questions.prompt: With an OpenAI Agents SDK session, what does the runner do around each run?

options.text: Loads the history before the run and stores new items after it
options.explanation: Right. That is why you don't call `to_input_list()` yourself when you use a session.

options.text: Sends only the newest user message and forgets everything before it
options.explanation: That describes no memory at all. A session keeps and reloads the conversation.

options.text: Writes a summary to `MEMORY.md` after every turn
options.explanation: That is closer to sandbox memory, which the OpenAI docs say is separate from session memory.

questions.prompt: Who runs the file operations of the Claude memory tool?

options.text: Anthropic's servers, in a managed memory store
options.explanation: The memory tool is client-side. Memory lives entirely in your application.

options.text: Your application, against storage you control
options.explanation: Right. Claude requests the operations; your handler executes them and must validate every path.
Claude only sends tool calls. Something outside the model has to read and write the files.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of structured note-taking from Anthropic's context engineering post?

options.explanation: The post says larger windows will still face context pollution. Notes live outside the window.

options.text: An agent keeping a NOTES.md file that it reads back later
options.explanation: Right. The agent writes notes outside the context window and pulls them back in when needed.

options.text: Sending the full chat history on every single call to the model
options.explanation: That is session history, and it grows every turn. Notes are a short, chosen record.
